narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist; sober, urgent storytelling, grave through the Passion.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; authoritative and prophetic in ch. 13, sorrowful yet resolute in the Passion, commanding after the Resurrection.

chief-priests.name: The chief priests
chief-priests.note: Temple leaders, here speaking together with the scribes; scheming in private, mocking at the cross.

bystanders.name: Bystanders
bystanders.note: Those standing by: pressing Peter in the courtyard; mishearing Jesus' cry at the cross.

pilate.name: Pontius Pilate
pilate.note: The Roman governor; cool, puzzled, half-mocking, yielding to the crowd.

crowd.name: The crowd
crowd.note: The multitude before Pilate, stirred up by the chief priests; shouting.

soldiers.name: The soldiers
soldiers.note: Roman soldiers of the band; coarse mock homage.

passers-by.name: Passers-by at the cross
passers-by.note: People passing Golgotha, wagging their heads and taunting.

bystander-with-sponge.name: Bystander with the sponge
bystander-with-sponge.note: One of those at the cross who runs to offer vinegar; curious, half-mocking.

centurion.name: The centurion
centurion.note: Roman officer facing the cross; awed confession.

1.t: And straightway in the morning the chief priests, holding a consultation with the ancients, and the Scribes, and the whole council, binding Jesus, led him away, and delivered him to Pilate.

2.t: Art thou the king of the Jews:
But he answering, saith to him:

3.t: And the chief priests accused him in many things.

4.t: And Pilate again asked him, saying:
Answerest thou nothing? behold in how many things they accuse thee.

5.t: But Jesus still answered nothing; so that Pilate wondered.

6.t: Now on the festival-day he was wont to release unto them one of the prisoners, whomsoever they demanded.

7.t: And there was one called Barabbas, who was put in prison with seditious men, who in the sedition had committed murder.

8.t: And when the multitude was come up, they began to desire that he would do as he had ever done to them.

9.t: And Pilate answered them, and said:
Will you that I release to you the king of the Jews?

10.t: For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him up through envy.

11.t: But the chief priests moved the people, that he should rather release Barabbas to them.

12.t: And Pilate again answering, saith to them:
What will you then that I do to the king of the Jews?

14.t: Why, what evil hath he done?
But they cried out the more:

15.t: So Pilate being willing to satisfy the people, released to them Barabbas, and delivered up Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.

16.t: And the soldiers led him into the court of the palace, and they called together the whole band.

17.t: And they clothe him with purple, and platting a crown of thorns, they put it upon him.

18.t: And they began to salute him:

19.t: And they struck his head with a reed: And they did spit on him, and bowing their knees, they worshipped him.

20.t: And after they had mocked him, they took off the purple from him, and put his own garments on him, and they led him out to crucify him.

21.t: And they forced one Simon, a Cyrenian, who passed by, coming out of the country, the father of Alexander, and of Rufus, to take up his cross.

22.t: And they bring him into the place called Golgotha, which being interpreted, is, The place of Calvary.

23.t: And they gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh: but he took it not.

24.t: And crucifying him, they divided his garments, casting lots upon them what every man should take.

25.t: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

26.t: And the inscription of his cause was written over: The King of the Jews.
26.q: the written inscription "The King of the Jews." is read by the narrator, not spoken by anyone

27.t: And with him they crucify two thieves; the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.

28.t: And the Scripture was fulfilled, which saith: And with the wicked he was reputed.

29.t: And they that passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads, and saying:
Vah, thou that destroyest the temple of God, and in three days buildest it up again:

30.t: Save thyself, coming down from the cross.

31.t: In like manner also the chief priests, with the Scribes, mocking, said one to another:
He saved others, himself he cannot save.
31.q: spoken by the chief priests with the scribes

32.t: Let Christ, the king of Israel, come down now from the cross, that we may see and believe.
And they that were crucified with him, reviled him.

33.t: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole earth, until the ninth hour.

34.t: And at the ninth hour, Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying:
which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
34.q: the translation "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" is the narrator's gloss per convention; could be voiced by Jesus

35.t: And some of the standers-by hearing, said:

36.t: And one running, and filling a sponge with vinegar, and putting it upon a reed, gave him to drink, saying:
Stay, let us see if Elias come to take him down.

37.t: And Jesus having cried out with a loud voice, gave up the ghost.

38.t: And the veil of the temple was rent in two, from the top to the bottom.

39.t: And the centurion who stood over-against him, seeing, that crying out in this manner, he had given up the ghost, said:
Indeed this man was the son of God.

40.t: And there were also women looking on afar off: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of James the less, and of Joseph; and Salome;

41.t: Who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered to him, and many other women that came up with him to Jerusalem.

42.t: And when evening was now come, (because it was the Parasceve, that is, the day before the sabbath),

43.t: Joseph, of Arimathea, a noble counsellor, who was also himself looking for the kingdom of God, came and went in boldly to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus.

44.t: But Pilate wondered that he should be already dead. And sending for the centurion, he asked him if he were already dead.

45.t: And when he had understood it by the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.

46.t: And Joseph buying fine linen, and taking him down, wrapped him up in the fine linen, and laid him in a sepulchre, which was hewed out of a rock, and he rolled a stone to the door of the sepulchre.

47.t: And Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of Joseph, beheld where he was laid.
